questions.q: Why does this lesson use a small base model and a modest dataset for the end-to-end pipeline run?
options: Because small models cannot be used with TRL at all
Because it makes the full three-stage pipeline actually feasible to run and inspect, for the purpose of seeing the dynamics work end-to-end rather than producing a production-quality model
Because reward models cannot be trained on large base models
Because PPO requires fewer than 100 training examples by design
questions.explain: The goal of a small-scale run is to make the pipeline's mechanics and dynamics observable and debuggable, not to reach production quality.

questions.q: In the PPO-based path shown, what is the reward model initialized from, and why?
options: A randomly initialized network with no connection to the SFT model
The SFT checkpoint (sft-small), because the reward model should be built on the same weights whose outputs it was trained to score, consistent with lesson 42
The DPO checkpoint, trained in a separate earlier run
The PPOTrainer's value head weights directly
questions.explain: Consistent with the pipeline wiring from lesson 42, the reward model is initialized from the SFT checkpoint so it's aligned with the policy distribution it will later score.

questions.q: What is the healthy pattern to watch for in PPO training logs, versus the early warning sign of reward hacking?
options: Loss decreasing is the only signal that matters; reward and KL are irrelevant
A rising mean reward alongside a flat or slowly rising KL divergence is healthy; a reward that spikes while KL explodes at the same time is an early sign of reward hacking
KL divergence should always be exactly zero throughout training
Reward should decrease steadily while KL increases
questions.explain: Watching reward and KL together, not reward alone, is how the lesson recommends catching the reward-hacking dynamic from lesson 44 early, before it gets worse.

questions.q: What is the DPO analog of PPO's 'reward trend' signal, and what should it look like in a healthy run?
options: There is no DPO analog; DPO produces no comparable training signal
The implicit reward margin (chosen minus rejected log-probability gap), which should climb steadily rather than jump erratically
The number of PPO rollouts collected per epoch
The reward model's held-out preference accuracy from lesson 40
questions.explain: Since DPO has no explicit reward model, its health signal is the implicit reward margin between chosen and rejected responses, which should increase steadily during a healthy run.

questions.q: Before trusting either trained policy (PPO-based or DPO), what sanity check does this lesson recommend?
options: Deploying the model directly to production with no further checks

Comparing its generations against the SFT baseline on held-out prompts and checking whether scores reflect genuine improvement rather than just longer or more confident wording (watching for verbosity bias)
Deleting the SFT checkpoint immediately after PPO or DPO training finishes
Only checking the final training loss value, ignoring generated text entirely
questions.explain: A held-out comparison against the SFT baseline, with an eye for verbosity bias from lesson 44, is the recommended way to confirm the trained policy actually improved rather than just gaming the scoring signal.
